subject: Connection matrix and ratecap request — FinLedger streaming pilot
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finledger.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: finite-state streaming pilot — connection matrix attachment

Thanks for the time this morning, Samira and Raj — good conversation. Attached is the connection matrix I promised (conn_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short Mutual Action Plan draft to kick off the pilot. Key points I captured from the call: 

- Pilot scope: 4-week proof-of-concept for realtime ledger enrichment (low-latency streaming) using your sandbox dataset.
- Expected steady-state: ~300 concurrent active sessions during business hours, with 850 peak parallel request bursts during end-of-day processing windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <= 200ms for short responses (<=128 tokens); p95 streaming chunk latency <= 80ms.
- Streaming model: server-sent-chunks over HTTP/2 (preferred) with optional websocket fallback for mobile clients.

Ask: please review the attached conn_matrix and highlight any session lifecycle behaviors we missed (session duration, keepalive, reconnect frequency). We'll propose rate caps and a dedicated pilot quota once we get your expected reconnect/backoff profile.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Samira: confirm typical session TTL and reconnection pattern by EOD Nov 2.
2) Redwood (Ben + Karthik): produce a pilot quota proposal and map to our Dedicated/reserved capacity options by Nov 3.
3) Legal/Procurement: engage DocuSign for a 30-day pilot order form (we can send a mini-SOW).

Attachments: conn_matrix_v1.xlsx, pilot_mutual_action_plan.pdf

--
Evelyn Hart
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finledger.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finledger.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: finite-state streaming pilot — connection matrix attachment

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciate the notes and the attachments. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Session TTL: average 18 minutes for interactive sessions; batch-style connectors open short-lived sessions (~30–90 seconds) during ingestion.
- Reconnects: mobile clients try exponential backoff; we see ~1.6 reconnects per session on average across regions.
- Peak window detail: the 850 parallel burst is short (5–12 minutes) but sustained QPS during that time can reach ~2,400 QPS aggregate.

One ask: can Redwood provide guidance on connection pooling semantics for our connectors? We need to know whether to multiplex multiple logical sessions over fewer physical sockets (we prefer multiplexing to conserve file descriptors on connectors).

Samira
VP Product, FinLedger
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finledger.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finledger.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: finite-state streaming pilot — connection matrix attachment

Samira — good data, thank you. Short answers up front: multiplexing is supported (HTTP/2 streams and websockets multiplexed over a single physical connection) and is recommended for your connectors; Redwood will count logical sessions for concurrency accounting, not physical sockets, with configurable socket affinity for sticky session needs.

Some preliminary numbers based on the matrix and your reconnection profile: 
- Pilot quota ask (initial): 400 reserved concurrent sessions, burst tokens to allow up to 1,000 parallel in 10-min windows for EOD flushes.
- Sustained tokenized rate: map 2,400 aggregate QPS to a mix of parallel requests + batching; recommend enabling automatic batching for small responses to keep p95 servicing stable.
- Streaming specifics: chunk-size target of 256 tokens, with server push aiming for sub-80ms chunk latency; we can route streaming over lower-latency region endpoints during your peak windows.

I'll attach a short excerpt of the Redwood ratecard for pilot SKUs and a first-pass connection matrix variant (see redwood-ratecard-excerpt.pdf). Evelyn / Karthik, I'll follow up with a formal quota proposal once Samira confirms a few connector details.

Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finledger.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connection matrix details + questions on keepalive and pooling

Hi all — quick technical follow-up from our infra/eng review. A few specific asks that will materially change the quota we propose: 

1) Keepalive/TTL semantics: do your connectors use HTTP keepalive with 60s TCP idle timeout, or do they frequently close sockets after each request? The former favors multiplexing; the latter increases socket churn.
2) Tokenization: do you expect many short completions (~<50 tokens) or intermittent longer generations? Short completions benefit more from caching/prefix reuse.
3) Backoff behavior: confirm exponential backoff floor and ceiling (e.g., min 50ms, max 5s) — this affects our burst smoothing and burst token modeling.

If you can share a small sample of connection logs (anonymized) we can generate a recommended concurrency map (sessions->sockets->burst tokens) and a pilot quota (reserved concurrent sessions + burst bucket). We'll include a small safety credit to cover unexpected reconnection storms.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finledger.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finledger.com>
Date: 2028-11-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connection matrix and ratecap request — FinLedger streaming pilot

Karthik / Ben — thanks for the clarity. We've pulled a short anonymized connector log slice (attached to this reply in Drive) and confirmed connector behavior:

- Keepalive: connectors use HTTP keepalive with a 90s idle timeout by default; mobile clients occasionally close sockets after each interaction.
- Token profile: ~65% short completions (<60 tokens), 35% longer (~200 tokens) during enrichment passes.
- Backoff: exponential with floor 100ms and ceiling 4s.

Based on your initial ask, FinLedger is comfortable with a pilot quota of 450 reserved concurrent sessions + 1,200 burst tokens (10-min window) for EOD surges. Please turn that into a formal quote (outline pricing impact, pilot billing terms) and we can sign the pilot SOW.

Samira
VP Product, FinLedger
